prompt: Define class `Model(name, size_gb)` storing both plus `loaded = False`, with `load()` setting loaded to True and `describe()` returning 'phi3:mini (2.2 GB)', or 'phi3:mini (2.2 GB, loaded)' once loaded.
check:
m, other = Model("phi3:mini", 2.2), Model("llama3:8b", 4.7)
assert m.loaded is False, m.loaded
assert m.describe() == "phi3:mini (2.2 GB)", m.describe()
m.load()
assert m.describe() == "phi3:mini (2.2 GB, loaded)", m.describe()
assert other.loaded is False, "loading one Model must not load another"
why: Instance state is assigned on self in __init__; every method takes self first.

prompt: Define class `Booking(room, start, end)` whose repr is `Booking('A', 9, 11)` (developer view, valid Python) and whose str is `Room A, 09:00-11:00` (user view).
check:
b = Booking("A", 9, 11)
assert repr(b) == "Booking('A', 9, 11)", repr(b)
assert str(b) == "Room A, 09:00-11:00", str(b)
assert f"{b}" == "Room A, 09:00-11:00", f"{b}"
assert str([b]) == "[Booking('A', 9, 11)]", "containers show each item's repr: " + str([b])
assert repr(Booking("O'Hare", 9, 10)) == 'Booking("O\'Hare", 9, 10)', "hand-written quotes break on O'Hare; use !r: " + repr(Booking("O'Hare", 9, 10))
why: __repr__ uses {x!r} so Python picks the quotes; __str__ is for print/f-strings; containers use repr.

prompt: Define class `Session(user)`: a class attribute `count` that counts every Session ever created, a per-instance `history` list, and `add(command)` appending to it.
check:
s1, s2 = Session("jack"), Session("becca")
s1.add("list")
assert s1.history == ["list"], s1.history
assert s2.history == [], "history is shared: a class-level [] is ONE list for every instance"
assert Session.count == 2, f"Session.count is {Session.count}"
assert "count" not in vars(s1), "self.count += 1 created a shadowing instance attr; bump Session.count"
why: Mutable state goes in __init__; bump shared counters via the class name, not self.

prompt: Define class `ModelSpec(name, size_gb)` with a static `parse_size(text)` ('2.2GB' -> 2.2, case-insensitive, GB only) and an alternate constructor `from_line(line)` building one from 'phi3:mini 2.2GB' (ValueError unless exactly 2 parts). Subclasses calling from_line must get a subclass instance.
why: @staticmethod takes no self/cls; @classmethod alternate constructors return cls(...) so subclasses work.

prompt: Define class `Room(capacity)` where `capacity` is a property: its setter raises ValueError unless the value is a positive int, and construction goes through the same check.
why: @property getter + @capacity.setter storing self._capacity; __init__ assigns self.capacity so it validates.

prompt: Define class `ModelRef(name, tag)` with value equality (name case-insensitive, tag case-sensitive) that also works as a set member / dict key. Comparing to a non-ModelRef must give False, not an error.
check:
a, b = ModelRef("Phi3", "mini"), ModelRef("phi3", "mini")
assert a == b and not (a != b), "same name (any case) + tag must be equal"
assert a != ModelRef("phi3", "MINI"), "tag is case-sensitive"
try:
    assert len({a, b, ModelRef("PHI3", "mini")}) == 1, "equal refs must hash equal"
except TypeError:
    raise AssertionError("unhashable: defining __eq__ set __hash__ to None, add __hash__") from None
assert {a: "small"}[ModelRef("PHI3", "mini")] == "small"
assert (a == "phi3:mini") is False
assert a.__eq__("phi3:mini") is NotImplemented, "return NotImplemented for other types, not False"
why: Defining __eq__ sets __hash__ = None; hash the same tuple you compare, and return NotImplemented for foreign types.

prompt: Define `PerishableItem(InventoryItem)` adding `days_left`. Its value() is the parent's value() when days_left > 2, half of it at 1-2, and 0.0 at <= 0. Reuse the parent's __init__ and value(); don't recompute price * qty.
check:
p = PerishableItem("MILK", 4.0, 3, days_left=5)
assert (p.sku, p.price, p.qty) == ("MILK", 4.0, 3), "call super().__init__(sku, price, qty)"
assert isinstance(p, InventoryItem)
assert p.value() == 12.0, p.value()
assert PerishableItem("A", 4.0, 3, 2).value() == 6.0, PerishableItem("A", 4.0, 3, 2).value()
assert PerishableItem("A", 4.0, 3, 0).value() == 0.0, PerishableItem("A", 4.0, 3, 0).value()
InventoryItem.value = lambda self: 100.0
assert PerishableItem("A", 1.0, 1, 5).value() == 100.0, "reuse super().value() instead of recomputing price * qty"
why: super().__init__(...) for shared fields; super().method() inside an override reuses the parent's logic.

prompt: Define abstract base `Provider` with class attribute `name = 'base'`, an abstract `fetch(city)`, and a concrete `report(city)` returning e.g. 'dict: Durham 21.5C' (self.name, city, temp to 1 decimal). Provider() and any subclass missing fetch must raise TypeError.
why: Subclass ABC and mark fetch @abstractmethod; the TypeError fires at instantiation, not class definition.

prompt: Define dataclass `Job(priority, name, tags)` sortable by (priority, name), where `tags` defaults to a fresh empty list per job and is ignored by == and ordering.
check:
j = Job(1, "chat")
j.tags.append("fast")
assert Job(2, "embed").tags == [], "each Job needs its own tags list (default_factory=list)"
assert repr(Job(1, "chat")) == "Job(priority=1, name='chat', tags=[])", repr(Job(1, "chat"))
jobs = sorted([Job(2, "b"), Job(1, "z", ["x"]), Job(1, "a")])
assert [(x.priority, x.name) for x in jobs] == [(1, "a"), (1, "z"), (2, "b")], jobs
assert Job(1, "a", ["x"]) == Job(1, "a", ["y"]), "tags must not affect == (compare=False)"
why: @dataclass(order=True) compares fields in definition order; mutable defaults need field(default_factory=list).

prompt: Define an immutable, hashable dataclass `Slot(start, end)` (ints) that raises ValueError at construction unless start < end.
why: frozen=True gives immutability and __hash__; __post_init__ runs after the generated __init__ for validation.

prompt: Define class `Version(text)` comparing numerically on its dotted parts ('1.10' > '1.9'), writing only __eq__, __lt__ and __hash__ by hand yet supporting <=, >, >=. Non-Version comparisons: == gives False, < raises TypeError.
check:
V = Version
assert V("1.10.0") > V("1.9.3"), "compare int tuples, not strings"
assert V("2.0") >= V("1.99"), ">= should come from @total_ordering"
assert V("1.0") <= V("1.0")
assert [v.key for v in sorted([V("1.10"), V("1.2"), V("1.9.1")])] == [(1, 2), (1, 9, 1), (1, 10)]
assert len({V("1.2"), V("1.2")}) == 1, "equal Versions must hash the same"
assert (V("1.0") == "1.0") is False
try:
    V("1.0") < "1.0"
except TypeError:
    pass
else:
    raise AssertionError("< against a str should raise TypeError (return NotImplemented)")
why: @functools.total_ordering fills in <=, >, >= from __eq__ + __lt__; keep __hash__ consistent with __eq__.

prompt: Define class `ModelRegistry(models)` over a list of {'name', 'size_gb'} dicts, supporting len(reg), `name in reg`, reg[name] (KeyError if unknown), and `for m in reg` yielding the dicts in insertion order.
why: __len__, __contains__, __getitem__, __iter__; without __iter__, for-loops fall back to reg[0], reg[1]...

prompt: Define context-manager class `ModelLease(name, log, swallow=())`: entering appends 'load <name>' and binds the lease to `as`; exiting ALWAYS appends 'unload <name>'. An exception from the body propagates unless it's an instance of a type in `swallow`.
check:
log = []
with ModelLease("phi3", log) as lease:
    assert isinstance(lease, ModelLease), "__enter__ must return self"
    log.append("ask")
assert log == ["load phi3", "ask", "unload phi3"], log
log = []
try:
    with ModelLease("phi3", log):
        raise ValueError("bad prompt")
except ValueError:
    pass
else:
    raise AssertionError("ValueError was swallowed: __exit__ must return False unless it's in swallow")
assert log == ["load phi3", "unload phi3"], log
try:
    with ModelLease("phi3", [], swallow=(LookupError,)):
        {}["missing"]
except KeyError:
    raise AssertionError("KeyError is a LookupError; swallow=(LookupError,) should suppress it")
why: __enter__ returns what `as` binds; __exit__ always runs, and returning True suppresses the exception.

prompt: Write `get(self, city)` (a top-level def; the check attaches it to ProviderClient): key = city stripped + lowercased; return the cached value if present, else call self.provider.fetch(key), retrying ONLY TimeoutError up to self.retries extra times and re-raising the last one. Cache successes only.
check:
ProviderClient.get = get
temps = {"durham": 21.5, "cary": 22.0}
p = FakeProvider(temps); c = ProviderClient(p)
assert c.get(" Durham ") == 21.5 and p.calls == ["durham"], p.calls
c.get("DURHAM")
assert len(p.calls) == 1, "second get should be a cache hit"
p = FakeProvider(temps, timeouts=2); c = ProviderClient(p, retries=2)
assert c.get("cary") == 22.0 and len(p.calls) == 3, f"2 timeouts + 1 success, got {len(p.calls)} calls"
p = FakeProvider(temps, timeouts=3); c = ProviderClient(p, retries=2)
try:
    c.get("cary")
except TimeoutError:
    pass
else:
    raise AssertionError("after 1 try + 2 retries, re-raise the TimeoutError")
assert len(p.calls) == 3, f"1 try + 2 retries, got {len(p.calls)} calls"
assert c.get("cary") == 22.0, "a failure must not be cached"
p = FakeProvider(temps); c = ProviderClient(p, retries=5)
try:
    c.get("boston")
except KeyError:
    pass
assert len(p.calls) == 1, f"only TimeoutError is retried, got {len(p.calls)} calls"
why: One seam owns retry + cache: loop over attempts, catch only the transient error, bare `raise` on the last try.
